length.note: VERIFIED, with one caveat noted below. Source is the official Moto Guzzi 850 Le Mans owner's manual (the original Mark 1/850 Le Mans manual, confirmed by its engine spec page matching the 1976 model exactly: 844cc, 83x78mm bore/stroke, '80 SAE at 7.300 r.p.m.' claimed output - the same 'optimistic' 80hp claim referenced by Guzzi historian Ian Falloon for the 1976 launch bike). Page 9 ('Dimensions and weights' section) literally reads: 'Wheelbase: 1.470 m / Max. width: 2.190 m / Max. length: 0.720 m'. As printed this is physically impossible (a max length shorter than the wheelbase, and a width wider than the whole bike), so the length/width labels and values have clearly been transposed somewhere in the original manual's translation/typesetting or in the scan-to-text extraction. The wheelbase value (1.470 m) matches independent sources almost exactly (bikez.com and others give 1470-1473 mm), which increases confidence the two mislabelled figures are also genuine factory values, just swapped. Corrected pairing (length=2.190 m/2190 mm, width=0.720 m/720 mm) is corroborated independently by the closely related later Le Mans IV (1993), whose documented dimensions are 2190 x 610 x 1210 mm (autoevolution) - i.e. the same ~2190 mm overall length recurs across the Le Mans lineage. Recommend treating 2190 mm as the length with this transposition explained, rather than shipping it as a clean, unqualified figure.

conventions.weight: Manufacturer-published dry/unladen weight (no fuel or fluids) is used wherever a source publishes one. For models where no manufacturer dry figure could be found (mostly modern bikes that only publish kerb/wet weight), the kerb or wet weight is used as a documented fallback, flagged per card below.
conventions.topSpeed: The manufacturer's claimed top speed is used wherever published. Where no claimed figure exists, the top speed recorded in a contemporary or well-corroborated independent road test is used instead, as noted per card below.
conventions.length: Overall (bumper-to-bumper) length is used wherever a genuine published figure exists. For eight models — mostly pre-1970s British bikes — no source (manufacturer literature, owners' clubs, museums, auction houses, workshop manuals) publishes an overall length figure at all, only wheelbase. For those eight cards only, wheelbase is used as a documented, clearly flagged fallback rather than an invented figure; every other card's length is genuine overall length. See each affected card's _sources.length.note below.
